title: demand.json _comment is corrupted: the W4 sentence-completion fix spliced a duplicate fragment mid-word
evidence: Eras 1/2 are UNCHANGED (dormant in the MVP — the shipped app starts at Foundations (era 1, USER RULING 20the shipped app starts at Foundations (era 1, USER RULING 2026-08-28) and advances via the 6.2 gate; the era-3 plans fire when the run reaches the Streaming Surge." — verified in the working tree via json.load: the substring 'RULING 20the shipped' is present. The commit message claims 'the demand comment sentence completed' but the replacement landed at the wrong offset inside the existing clause.
detail: The catalog's permanent documentation now carries a garbled duplicated clause; the commit over-claims this fix as done.
recommended_fix: Rewrite the tail as one clean sentence: "...the shipped app starts at Foundations (era 1, USER RULING 2026-08-28) and advances via the 6.2 gate; the era-3 plans fire when the run reaches the Streaming Surge."

title: econ unit test silently passes when catalogs fail to load, contradicting its own anti-vacuity purpose and the sibling pattern
detail: A load failure (wrong cwd, missing data/) prints to stderr and returns — the test ships green with zero assertions run, recreating the vacuity the file's header says it prevents.
recommended_fix: Replace print+return with testing.fail_now(t, fmt.tprintf("econ unit: catalog load failed: %s", e)), matching the a11y oracle test's pattern.

title: Tautological sanity assertion: stats.crises >= 0 can never fail on an i32
evidence:
testing.expectf(t, stats.crises >= 0, "sanity")
Field declaration (harness/econ.odin:41):
	crises:          i32, // Crisis_Triggered events (the literal 4.2 crisis seam, W3)
detail: A signed int is always >= 0; the assertion adds no coverage and noise to a gate whose whole point is biting.
recommended_fix: Delete the sanity line, or assert a real property (e.g. the era-2 brush fires zero crises: stats.crises == 0).

title: saw_crisis_active latch conjunct is dominated by the live crisis check — simpler one-conjunct guard gives the identical counts
detail: Triggers always precede same-tick dots in the buffer and earlier-tick walks latch already, so whenever the live check is true the latch is true — the first conjunct never alters the outcome.
recommended_fix: Guard on len(s.crisis.active) > 0 alone and delete the saw_crisis_active field plus both latch writes; same counts, less machinery.
